# Maximum Number of Balloons.

@example Two each of b, a and n and four each of l and o make two strands; the x is left over.
"olnabxolbalonol"
=> 2

@example b, a, n and the four o would allow two strands, but three l make only one pair.
"lobnaxlaboonlo"
=> 1

@example All five letters are there, but only one l and one o, and a strand needs two of each.
"bagelon"
=> 0

# A single letter.
"b"
=> 0

# The word itself.
"balloon"
=> 1

# Every letter once: only one l and one o.
"qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm"
=> 0

# Enough for three strands except for one letter, which allows only two:
# b, then a, then n.
"bllblalonaoooaltnolokn"
=> 2

"nlolbbnaoonlolalboleo"
=> 2

"olnpobwlnbblollaooaola"
=> 2

# Five l (or five o) make only two pairs: halve and round down.
"onlobaalnbooonlolalb"
=> 2

"nbullalobnlaoalboolon"
=> 2

# A single l stops everything, however many of the rest there are.
"boononmolbbbnooanaoaoa"
=> 0

# One letter repeated.
"llllllllllllllllllllllllllllll"
=> 0

# 257 b: a one-byte count would wrap to 1 and wrongly limit the answer.
"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbblbbbbbbbbbbbbabbbbbblbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbblbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbnbbbbbbbblbbbbbbbbbbbbbbabbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbabobbblbbbbbobbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbobbbbbbbbbbnobbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbobobbbblbbbbbbbbbnbbbbbb"
=> 3

# 10^4 letters: 1428 strands, with an odd 2857 of both l and o, and a q
# and a z left over.
""
=> 1428

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"aoolanenloobol"
=> 1

@gen 2 small
"oo"
=> 0

@gen 3 small
"olaobololabolnanllblb"
=> 2

@gen 4 small
"noblabxlnoaollonobalol"
=> 3

@gen 5 small
"bnlooloo"
=> 0

@gen 6 small
"olblaln"
=> 0
